title: Govern a workspace: who can endorse, and where labels end up
objective_text: Work out twelve governance outcomes: who may promote, certify or mark Master data, and which sensitivity label each item and export ends up with after a label change.
scenario: The Sales lakehouse is about to be shared across the company. Governance asked the team to endorse it properly and raise its label to Confidential, and wants to know beforehand exactly which items will carry which label.
engine_label: A model of endorsement rights and label inheritance, checked on this PC
verifies: Your answers follow the endorsement overview (who can promote, certify and mark Master data, and which items can't be endorsed) and the information protection and downstream inheritance pages (autogenerated items, create-from inheritance, manual and more restrictive labels kept, export paths), checked against a model on this PC.
does_not_verify: That any label or badge is applied: nothing runs here and no label policy is read.
Fully automated downstream inheritance, inheritance from data sources and default or mandatory labeling, which this exercise leaves out.
Label protection settings such as encryption, and what a label does to access in other tenants.

expected.description: Allowed: promote_lakehouse true, the other four false. Labels: sql_endpoint, notebook_created_from_lakehouse, model_unlabelled and report_pdf_export Confidential; model_manual_general General; model_highly_confidential Highly Confidential; csv_export none.

validation.pass: You know who can endorse what.

rules.why: Any user with write permissions on an item can promote it.
Only users a Fabric administrator specifies can certify. Being a workspace Admin isn't enough.
Master data only goes on items that contain data, such as lakehouses and semantic models.
Any Fabric or Power BI item except Power BI dashboards can be promoted or certified.

validation.pass: A label must be published to the user.

rules.why: Being in the specified users list isn't enough. The label must also be published to the user in a label policy.

validation.fail: Some items don't end up with the label you'd expect from inheritance.
validation.pass: You know which items take the lakehouse's new label.

rules.why: Autogenerated items from a lakehouse take their label from the parent lakehouse.
A notebook created from a lakehouse inherits the lakehouse's label.
Downstream inheritance is on by default and goes from Fabric items to Power BI items.
Downstream inheritance never overwrites a label that was applied manually.
Downstream inheritance never replaces a label with a less restrictive one.

validation.fail: The exports don't carry the labels you said.
validation.pass: You know which exports keep the label.

rules.why: Export to PDF is one of the export paths where a label stays with the data.
Export to .csv isn't a supported path, so the file leaves without the label.

hints: Who can promote, and who decides who can certify?
What kind of item can be Master data?
Which items take a lakehouse's label without anyone choosing it?
When does downstream inheritance leave a label alone?
Which export paths keep the label?
explanation: Promoted is for anyone with write permission. Certified and Master data are only for users a Fabric administrator specifies, and Master data only fits items that contain data. Power BI dashboards can't be endorsed. To apply a label, a user must be allowed to label in Fabric and have the label published to them. When the lakehouse becomes Confidential, its autogenerated SQL analytics endpoint takes the parent's label, a notebook created from it inherits it, and downstream inheritance carries it to an unlabelled semantic model. Downstream inheritance never overwrites a manual label and never lowers a label, so the General model and the Highly Confidential model keep theirs. Export to PDF keeps the label, and export to .csv doesn't.
review_notes: Checked on Learn 2026-11-20: endorsement-overview (any user with write permissions can promote; any Fabric or Power BI item except Power BI dashboards can be promoted or certified; only users specified by a Fabric administrator can certify or apply Master data, and only if an administrator enabled them; Master data only on items that contain data, such as lakehouses and semantic models). information-protection (labels must be published to the user, not just the specified users list; downstream inheritance on by default, Fabric to Fabric and Fabric to Power BI supported; autogenerated items take the parent lakehouse or warehouse label; a notebook created from a lakehouse inherits its label; labels stay with export to Excel, PDF and PowerPoint; access control on other export paths such as .csv is unsupported, and no other Fabric experience transfers the label on export). service-security-sensitivity-label-downstream-inheritance (never overwrites manually applied labels; never replaces with a less restrictive label; user consent mode needs edit permission on downstream items; limited to 80 items).

Not graded: mandatory labeling for lakehouses (the page says it isn't enforced unless the experience itself requires a label), and default labeling. The setup fixes the workspace, role and item count so the user consent rules hold.
